name: Peavine Mountain
summary: Mono forest and Grazing Service lookout on Peavine Mountain near Reno, opened 1942; closed 1970 by smog per one paper; no longer standing, removal date unknown.
design: Standard 14-by-14-foot lookout building with sleeping quarters, on a lookout tower
status_note: The 2012 report says it is no longer standing and does not know when it was removed. A 1970 newspaper item reports closure for smog.
agency: Mono National Forest with the U.S. Grazing Service (1942); the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest stewards the mountain today

access.note: Many miles of hiking and mountain bike trails have been added under Humboldt-Toiyabe stewardship; access from northwest Reno has become more restricted

visit.trail_note: A road winds up the north and east faces to the radio sites on the summit

events.note: Grazing Service crews built the station house and lookout tower; the Forest Service supplied the 14-by-14-foot building, which came from a Susanville site; a five-mile road was built to the summit
Station placed in operation July 21, 1942, with J.P. Ryan of the Mono forest service assigned to the post
Reno Evening Gazette item names Mrs. Jean Ferguson of Carson City as the person running the station
2012 report gives 1964 as the year the lookout was abandoned; the 1970 closure item does not agree
Nevada State Journal reports that smog forced the closure of the lookout
Still standing in 1972, according to the 2012 report
